newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta book fair destroyed by blaze.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta book fair destroyed by blaze.

text.p: A raging fire destroyed an international book fair in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta on Monday, reducing to ashes thousands of volumes at a make-shift exhibition site, fire brigade officials said.

Fire officials said at least four people suffered burns. They said the fire broke out at about 3:30 p.m. (1000 GMT) at the Calcutta Book Fair in the city's central Maidan area and was sparked by a kerosene stove in a dining hall.
Firefighters were still battling the fire an hour after it started, witnesses said.
The cluster of temporary structures made of wood, bamboo and tin which housed the book fair was destroyed, fire officials said. No estimate of damage was immediately available.

The book fair, which began last Wednesday and was scheduled to close on February 12, had adopted France as its theme and set up a miniature reproduction of Paris's Montmartre area featuring painters and musicians.
British and German publishers were among the major participants in the fair, which had more than 450 stalls.
